Mathews studied at St. Mark's Hospital London during the winter of 1877-1878, then returned to Kentucky and limited his practice to diseases of the colon and rectum. Pre-1950 observational_study. Content-match confirmed: Janssen DF. 'American Proctology Before 1899, Part 2: The Rise of the Rectal Specialists.' Dis Colon Rectum. 2021;64(12):1454-1462. PMID 34747915 abstract explicitly documents Mathews' St. Mark's study in the 1877-1878 winter, followed by his heading of a Special Commission on Rectal Diseases at the Kentucky State Medical Society (April 1878). The prior citation (PMID 23997672, Schoetz, a board-certification history) did not content-match the St. Mark's training fact. 34747915 already backs the Kentucky founder edge in-graph. Re-added onto the consolidated canonical node Joseph McDowell Mathews (was Joseph M. Mathews).
